data.title: Maine Senator Susan M. Collins Honored by Largest Kidney Patient Group
data.description:
Maine Senator Susan M. Collins Honored by Largest Kidney Patient Group

Maine Senator Susan M. Collins Honored by Largest Kidney Patient Group

PR Newswire

WASHINGTON, Oct. 30, 2026

Award Cites Courage to Transform Status Quo Patient Care Through Science

Federal Policy and Research Advance Innovation and Organ Transplantation

WASHINGTON, Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The American Association of Kidney Patients (AAKP), the nation's oldest and largest independent, non-partisan kidney patient advocacy organization, today announced it has awarded U.S. Senator Susan M. Collins of the State of Maine its 2026 National Leadership Award for Science and Medical Innovation. Collins chairs the powerful U.S. Senate Committee on Appropriations and serves on the Senate Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions (HELP), including the Primary Health and Retirement Security Subcommittee. The AAKP award cited Senator Collins for her "courage to transform status quo kidney, heart, and metabolic disease care through patient-centered policy and unyielding support for American science, innovation, and organ donation reform."

Kidney disease impacts more than 37 million Americans and their families. In the State of Maine, based on the U.S. Renal Data System (USRDS), there are over 228,000 people living with diseases, over 2,000 living with kidney failure, over 1,400 living on either in-center or home dialysis, and an additional 700 living with a kidney transplant. Across New England, including Maine, it is estimated that over 6,000 people are on the kidney transplant wait list. Nationwide, interrelated cardiovascular, kidney, and metabolic diseases have impacted more than 25% of the adult population and are a leading cause of death. More broadly, an estimated 90% of American adults, or approximately 240 million people, have some degree of interconnected cardiovascular, kidney, or metabolic health conditions according to the American Heart Association.

AAKP President Edward V. Hickey III, a chronic kidney disease patient with family ties to Bar Harbor, said: "AAKP has a long history of policy collaboration with the U.S. Congress, and we have tremendous respect for Senator Collins and her decades-long commitment to building America's research and science capacity, particularly at federal agencies like the National Institutes of Health and at the academic institutions leading work on kidney, cardiac, and metabolic diseases. Her leadership on patient-centered medicine and medical innovation has had, and continues to have, a profound impact on the lives of kidney and other chronic disease patients in Maine and across the nation. Without taxpayer-funded federal investment in kidney science and medicine, patients' choices and their access to new, life-saving innovations would be far more limited than they are today." Hickey is a U.S. Marine Corps veteran and a former senior Congressional aide. He serves on the American Board of Internal Medicine's (ABIM) Nephrology Specialty Board, is a patient advisor for multiple clinical trials administered by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, and chairs the AAKP Veterans Health Initiative, the largest kidney health outreach program outside of the VA.

Paul T. Conway, AAKP Vice President and Chair of Policy and Global Affairs, a 49-year kidney patient and 29-year kidney transplant recipient with roots in Bath and Belfast, Maine, stated, "Bipartisan Congressional legislation and federal appropriations, together with greater innovation, are transforming early kidney disease detection, treatment, and organ transplantation in Maine and nationally. Senator Collins has been steadfast in her commitment to improve cardiac, kidney, and diabetes research and to reduce patient and family burdens associated with chronic diseases. The federal research efforts she has championed, including those made through the National Institutes of Health and other federal agencies, have resulted in greater life-saving treatment choices for vulnerable people living in rural and urban areas." Conway is a University of Maine alumnus, former Chief of Staff of the U.S. Department of Labor, and past Chair of the U.S. Food and Drug Administration's Patient Engagement Advisory Committee (PEAC). He was diagnosed with kidney disease during a routine high school sports physical by his primary care physician, the late Dr. Peter M. Jollie of Belfast, Maine. Dr. Jollie, a retired Royal Air Force Flight Surgeon and veteran of the U.S. government's U2 aerospace programs, was a proponent of early disease screening and prevention.

AAKP advocates help kidney community efforts, coordinated by the American Society of Nephrology (ASN) (view report), to expand Congressional appropriations and taxpayer investments in kidney science and research by up to $1.8 billion, through the National Institutes of Health and the U.S. Department of Defense. Apart from the national impacts across a wide range of heart, kidney, and metabolic research issues, NIH-approved and taxpayer-supported research, science, and training grants have also directly benefited Maine. NIH grants in Maine have supported research related to metabolic conditions including diabetes, with spillovers to aspects of obesity, as well as medical student training in kidney function and diseases through the MDI Biological Institute in Bar Harbor, Maine. Other institutions receiving NIH funding for rural health and conditions such as cancer include The Jackson Laboratories and MaineHealth. In September of 2026, MaineHealth was awarded a five-year, $13.2 million Centers of Biomedical Research Excellence (COBRE) grant by the National Institute of General Medical Sciences of the National Institutes of Health. The funding will be used to further develop the COBRE in Acute Care Research and Rural Health established by the MaineHealth Institute for Research.

AAKP kicked off its 2026 award recognition cycle on September 10 at the William J. Clinton Presidential Center in Little Rock, Arkansas, during its annual National Patient Meeting with the unveiling of the national Kidney Advocate Hall of Fame. The AAKP Kidney Advocate Hall of Fame showcases advocates and medical professionals whose contributions have forever changed kidney medicine and launches a tradition that will honor individuals whose dedication continues to define excellence in kidney advocacy. AAKP provides advocacy skills and social media training for patients, living organ donors, and families through the AAKP Center for Patient Engagement and Advocacy and an allied network of government affairs and policy experts.

AAKP, alongside a broad coalition of patient organizations, transplant experts, and Congressional allies, is working to secure passage of the bipartisan Living Donor Protection Act (LDPA), S. 1552/H.R. 4582 and H.R. 4583. The legislation protects living organ donors from job and insurance discrimination based solely on their decision to donate a kidney to save another life, barriers cited most often by potential organ donors. The bipartisan bill is led by Senator Tom Cotton (R-AR) and Senator Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY). It was voted out of the Senate HELP Committee on February 26, 2026, with full bipartisan support, including Senator Susan Collins (R-ME), the endorsement of AAKP, the united kidney community, and the American Council of Life Insurance (ACLI). In 2018, with bipartisan support from both Congress and the White House, AAKP and transplant professionals worked with the U.S. Department of Labor's (DOL) legal team and the DOL Wage and Hour Division to have DOL extend Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) protections for living organ donors, based on the original intent of the FMLA's Congressional co-sponsors (click here to read the letter and click here to watch the video). Congressional passage of the LDPA in 2026 will codify the DOL's 2018 FMLA job protections and prohibit insurers from discriminating against living donors.

Follow AAKP on social media at @kidneypatient on Facebook, @kidneypatients on X, and @kidneypatients on Instagram, and visit http://www.aakp.org for more information. AAKP patient advocates advance bipartisan kidney policy including: passage of the bipartisan law modernizing the Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network (OPTN) (2023); lifetime transplant drug coverage for kidney patients (2020); the historic Executive Order on Advancing American Kidney Health signed by President Donald Trump (2019); job protections for living organ donors under the Family Medical Leave Act (FMLA) via the U.S. Department of Labor (2018); and Congressional approval of HIV positive organ transplants for HIV positive patients (2013). AAKP is committed to American leadership in the discovery of safe, next-generation kidney technologies while counteracting the pacing threat of China and its efforts to dominate biotech, manipulate the drug supply chain, and limit patient choice.

data.title: NEXE Innovations Reports Q1 Fiscal 2027 Results and Business Update
data.description:
WINDSOR, Ontario, Oct. 30, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- NEXE Innovations Inc. ("NEXE", the "Company", "we", "us" or "our") (TSX.V: NEXE) (Frankfurt: NX5) (OTC: NEXNF), a compostable and innovative materials company, is pleased to announce its financial results for the three-month period ended August 31, 2026 ("Q1 2027").

NEXE grew revenue 10.5% to $133,119 in Q1 2027 from $120,484 in Q1 2026, in a quarter that has, in management's view, been historically seasonally soft for the North American coffee industry, and reduced its net loss 33.7% to $(946,396). During the quarter, NEXE began deliveries to an East Coast fair-trade organic coffee co-operative that previously had no single-serve offering and onboarded a U.S. coffee chain with locations in New York City and Boston. Based on current customer interest and commercial opportunities in progress, management currently expects annual pod volumes to exceed the upper end of the previously announced range of 10 to 15 million compostable coffee pods.

Results for the quarter also reflect higher costs. Gross loss was $(47,552), compared to gross income of $16,453 in the three-month period ended August 31, 2025 ("Q1 2026"), and the net loss improvement was, in management's view, primarily attributable to lower depreciation, including the effect of a change in depreciation estimates.

Q1 2027 Highlights

  • Revenue: $133,119, up 10.5% from $120,484 in Q1 2026, in a quarter that has historically been seasonally soft.

  • Net loss: $(946,396), or $(0.01) per share, an improvement of 33.7%, with total operating expenses down 37.4%.

  • Customers: Deliveries began to Just Us! Coffee Roasters, a U.S. coffee chain was onboarded, and the Company is in discussions with a U.S. brand regarding potential distribution to a national hotel chain.

  • Volume outlook: Based on current customer interest and commercial opportunities in progress, management currently expects annual pod volumes to exceed the upper end of the previously announced range of 10 to 15 million pods.

  • Liquidity: Cash, cash equivalents, GICs and term deposits of $8,008,095 and working capital of $7,693,960.

"Revenue grew 10.5% in what has historically been a seasonally soft quarter, and we began deliveries to new customers during the period," said Ash Guglani, President of NEXE. "Gross margin in the quarter reflected the costs of onboarding those customers, which we believe may trend lower as volumes build. Our focus for the rest of fiscal 2027 is to convert our commercial pipeline into production volume."

Q1 2027 Financial Results

  • Revenue Growth: Revenue was $133,119, compared to $120,484 in Q1 2026, reflecting repeat orders from existing customers and new customers onboarded during the quarter. Shipments were weighted to July and August 2026. The first quarter has historically been seasonally weak, and management believes coffee sales across the industry typically decline during the summer months.

  • Gross Margin: Gross loss was $(47,552), compared to gross income of $16,453 in Q1 2026, as cost of goods sold increased 73.7% to $180,671 from $104,031. Management believes the increase reflects higher volumes, onboarding costs for new customers, higher packaging costs, a larger share of pods filled with coffee purchased by the Company, $54,742 of non-cash production depreciation (recorded in operating expenses in Q1 2026) and $10,685 of inventory write-downs. Management expects that costs will trend lower as volumes increase, as management expects higher volumes will help absorb fixed costs and support bulk purchasing of materials.

  • Operating Expenses: Total operating expenses decreased 37.4% to $950,956 from $1,520,057, and operating loss before other items improved 33.6% to $(998,508) from $(1,503,604). Depreciation in operating expenses decreased 75.9% to $108,103. Effective June 1, 2026, the Company extended the estimated useful lives of its metered production machinery and changed the depreciation method from straight-line to units of use, which reduced Q1 2027 depreciation by $269,353 relative to the previous estimates. Share-based compensation decreased 94.0% to $13,187 and research and development expenses decreased 67.7% to $33,447. Selling, general and administrative expenses increased 7.4% to $790,139, mainly due to higher compensation-related costs and higher legal and professional fees, partially offset by lower management fees, salaries, consulting fees, and advertising and promotion.

  • Net Loss: Net loss improved 33.7% to $(946,396), or $(0.01) per share, from $(1,427,807), or $(0.01) per share, in Q1 2026. The $481,411 improvement reflects lower depreciation, share-based compensation and research and development expenses, partially offset by the gross loss, higher selling, general and administrative expenses, and lower interest income.

  • Balance Sheet: As at August 31, 2026, NEXE had cash and cash equivalents of $3,875,352, investments in GICs of $4,102,743 and term deposits of $30,000, for a total of $8,008,095. Working capital was $7,693,960 (May 31, 2026 – $8,464,675), or $6.0 million excluding $1.7 million of prepayments on manufacturing equipment. Cash used in operating activities was $1,096,265 (Q1 2026 – $760,265), mainly reflecting operating expenditures and working capital movements, including a reduction in trade and other payables and an increase in trade and other receivables.

Commercial Update: Management Expects Annual Pod Volumes to Exceed 15 Million

NEXE supplied partners across retail, office coffee services and online channels during Q1 2027, and the previously disclosed partner transition continued through the quarter. NEXE continues to see increased interest in the compostable pod.

During the quarter, NEXE began deliveries to Just Us! Coffee Roasters, an East Coast fair-trade organic coffee co-operative that previously had no single-serve offering, and onboarded a U.S. coffee chain with multiple locations, including New York City and Boston. NEXE is in discussions with a U.S. brand regarding the potential supply of pods for distribution to a national hotel chain and is procuring materials for a new Canadian client.

Management currently expects annual pod volumes to exceed 15 million compostable coffee pods. NEXE anticipates current finished goods capacity aligns with expected production for the coming months and that capacity could be scaled with limited additional investment, such as larger molds or additional staff. The Company is also evaluating strategic opportunities that management anticipates would accelerate commercialization and enhance shareholder value, including potential partnerships, licensing arrangements, and other capital-efficient growth initiatives.

The Company's unaudited condensed consolidated interim financial statements for the three months ended August 31, 2026 and related management's discussion and analysis are available on NEXE's SEDAR+ profile at www.sedarplus.ca and the Company's website at www.nexeinnovations.com.

Our flagship product, the NEXE Pod, a BPI-certified compostable coffee pod, showcases our material's durability and is an ideal substitute for plastic. data.title: Mission Valley Bancorp Reports Third Quarter Results
data.description:
Mission Valley Bancorp Reports Third Quarter Results

Mission Valley Bancorp (OTCQX: MVLY, “Mission Valley”, or the “Company”) announced today net income of $1.2 million, or $0.36 per diluted share, for the third quarter of 2026, compared to net income of $2.1 million, or $0.62 per diluted share, for the third quarter of 2025. Net income for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $3.8 million, or $1.11 per diluted share, compared to net income of $4.9 million, or $1.45 per diluted share, for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

Tamara Gurney, Chief Executive Officer of Mission Valley Bancorp, commented, “We are pleased with the year-to-date growth of $15.2 million, or 10.1% annualized, in our non-interest bearing core deposits, particularly during a very challenging time to attract and retain core deposits for the industry as a whole. This supported gross loan growth of $6.4 million, after selling $13.4 million in SBA loan principal, for the current quarter. However, the most significant highlight of the quarter was the leadership transition at Mission Valley Bank with Brian Carlson being appointed President and Chief Executive Officer of Mission Valley Bank as I stepped in to the role of Executive Chair and CEO of Mission Valley Bancorp. Brian will be instrumental in shaping the path forward for the Company and the Bank.”

Brian Carlson, President and Chief Executive Officer of Mission Valley Bank and President of Mission Valley Bancorp, commented, “We were able to produce solid net income of $1.2 million, or $0.36 per diluted share, for the quarter despite the impact from the industry-wide headwinds on SBA lending volume and the increase in our provision for credit losses primarily due to one charged-off commercial loan. The quality of our SBA loan portfolio remains strong with low levels of past due, non-accrual, classified loans, and overall default rates that continue to outperform industry averages. In addition, secondary market premiums on SBA loans remain at favorable levels as we continue to grow the SBA loan portfolio, while maintaining our asset quality.”

Mr. Carlson continued, “As we look ahead to the fourth quarter and closing out 2026, we look forward to the full launch of one of our digital transformation initiatives and we will be focused on executing certain strategic and proactive measures with respect to our loan and investment portfolios to reposition and strengthen our balance sheet for 2027 and beyond.”

Third Quarter 2026 Highlights

  • Net Income of $1.2 million, or $0.36 per diluted share, for the third quarter of 2026.
  • Net Interest Income was $8.4 million for the third quarter of 2026, an increase of $0.5 million, or 7.01%, compared to the third quarter of 2025.
  • Net Interest Margin was 4.47% for the third quarter of 2026 compared to 4.54% for the third quarter of 2025.
  • Non-Interest Income was $2.3 million for the third quarter of 2026, a decrease of $0.5 million, or 17.98%, compared to the third quarter of 2025. Non-Interest Income includes gain on sale of loans and the change in the fair value of Small Business Administration (“SBA”) servicing assets.
  • $13.4 million in loan principal sold resulting in gain on sale of $0.8 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $17.9 million in loan principal sold and gain on sale of $0.9 million in the third quarter of 2025.
  • Change in the fair value of SBA servicing assets resulted in a net loss of $0.2 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to a net gain of $0.1 million in the third quarter of 2025.

Balance Sheet Highlights

  • Total Assets were $790.2 million as of September 30, 2026, an increase of $29.8 million, or 3.92%, compared to December 31, 2025.
  • Gross Loans were $637.1 million as of September 30, 2026, an increase of $27.5 million, or 4.51%, compared to December 31, 2025.
  • Total Deposits were $648.4 million as of September 30, 2026, an increase of $12.9 million, or 2.03%, compared to December 31, 2025. The $12.9 million growth in Total Deposits was driven by the $15.2 million increase in non-interest bearing deposits, partially offset by the $2.3 million decrease in interest bearing deposits.

Asset Quality

  • $397 thousand in net charge-offs on loans in the third quarter of 2026 primarily from one commercial loan, compared to $60 thousand in net recoveries from previously charged-off loans in the third quarter of 2025.
  • $13.0 million in Non-Accrual Loans as of September 30, 2026, compared to $9.2 million in Non-Accrual Loans as of December 31, 2025. As of September 30, 2026, Non-Accrual Loans were comprised of $6.3 million from commercial loans, $4.8 million from accounts receivable loans, and $1.9 million from SBA loans.
  • $33.1 million in Classified Loans as of September 30, 2026, compared to $16.7 million in Classified Loans as of December 31, 2025. As of September 30, 2026, Classified Loans were comprised of $15.4 million from accounts receivable loans, $8.4 million from commercial loans loans, $7.5 million from real estate loans, and $1.8 million from SBA loans.
  • $10.5 million in Past Due Loans as of September 30, 2026, compared to $15.6 million in Past Due Loans as of December 31, 2025. As of September 30, 2026, Past Due Loans were comprised of $5.2 million from commercial loans, $4.8 million from accounts receivable loans, and $0.5 million from SBA loans.
  • Provision for Credit Losses was $0.5 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $0.1 million in the third quarter of 2025. The provision in the third quarter of 2026 was primarily driven by the charge-off of one commercial loan.
  • The Allowance for Credit Losses was $8.4 million, or 1.32% of Gross Loans, as of September 30, 2026, compared to $8.1 million, or 1.33% of Gross Loans, as of December 31, 2025.

Capital and Liquidity

  • Capital position remains strong, which is reflected by Common Equity Tier 1 Capital Ratio of 10.31%, Tier 1 Capital ratio of 11.14%, Total Risk Based Capital Ratio of 12.33%, and Leverage Ratio of 10.07%.
  • Available borrowing capacity of $214.3 million as of September 30, 2026, a decrease of $9.0 million, or 4.03%, compared to December 31, 2025.
  • Unpledged available-for-sale investment securities of $40.3 million as of September 30, 2026.

About Mission Valley Bancorp

Mission Valley Bancorp is a bank holding company headquartered in Sun Valley, California with two wholly owned subsidiaries Mission Valley Bank (the "Bank") and Mission SBA Loan Servicing LLC (“Mission SBA”). The Bank was founded in 2001 and is a full-service, independent, commercial bank specializing in the banking needs of small to medium businesses with full-service branches in the San Fernando, Santa Clarita, and San Gabriel Valleys. Mission SBA is a de novo SBA lender service provider (“LSP”) established in March 2021 that provides SBA lending services to other financial institutions.

RICHMOND MUTUAL BANCORPORATION, INC. ANNOUNCES 2026 THIRD QUARTER FINANCIAL RESULTS

RICHMOND MUTUAL BANCORPORATION, INC. ANNOUNCES 2026 THIRD QUARTER FINANCIAL RESULTS

PR Newswire

RICHMOND, Ind., Oct. 30, 2026

RICHMOND, Ind., Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Richmond Mutual Bancorporation, Inc., a Maryland corporation (the "Company") (NASDAQ: RMBI), parent company of First Bank Midwest, today reported net income of $1.7 million, or diluted earnings per share of $0.11, for the third quarter of 2026. This compares to net income of $2.2 million, or $0.22 diluted earnings per share, for the second quarter of 2026, and net income of $3.6 million, or diluted earnings per share of $0.36, for the third quarter of 2025.

The decrease in net income from the second quarter of 2026 and the third quarter of 2025 was primarily due to higher provision for credit losses, as well as noninterest expense. The provision for credit losses totaled $6.1 million during the third quarter of 2026, compared to $823,000 in the prior quarter and $269,000 in the third quarter of 2025. The increase in provision was primarily due to the need to replenish and increase the allowance for credit losses following $6.1 million of net charge-offs during the quarter, including a partial charge-off of $4.5 million on a nonaccruing commercial real estate loan, which was transferred to other real estate owned during the current quarter, and an $803,000 charge-off on a commercial and industrial loan, as well as an increase in non-performing loans. In addition, noninterest expense during the quarter included $3.0 million of nonrecurring merger-related expenses associated with the acquisition of Farmers Bancorp. These items were partially offset by a preliminary bargain purchase gain recognized on the Company's acquisition of Farmers Bancorp of $1.6 million.

Net income for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $6.8 million, or $0.56 diluted earnings per share, compared to net income of $8.2 million, or $0.82 diluted earnings per share, for the same period in 2025.

On July 1, 2026, the Company completed its previously announced merger with Farmers Bancorp pursuant to the Agreement and Plan of Merger dated November 11, 2025. Immediately thereafter, The Farmers Bank merged with and into First Bank Richmond. The combined company continues to operate as Richmond Mutual Bancorporation, Inc., while the combined bank is operating under the name First Bank Midwest. The combined company continues to trade on the Nasdaq Capital Market under the ticker symbol "RMBI." The administrative headquarters of the holding company remains in Richmond, Indiana, while the combined bank is headquartered in Frankfort, Indiana.

The financial results presented in this earnings release reflect the Company's operations following the completion of the merger on July 1, 2026.  Accordingly, the Company's financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, include the operating results of the combined company. Financial results for periods prior to July 1, 2026, reflect the operations of Richmond Mutual Bancorporation, Inc., on a standalone basis, and do not include the operations of Farmers Bancorp.

Message from the Chairman and CEO

Garry Kleer, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, commented, "Our third quarter results reflected the impact of our merger with Farmers Bancorp, which significantly expanded our balance sheet and increased net interest income compared to both the prior quarter and the third quarter of last year. Earnings were impacted by a higher provision for credit losses and increased noninterest expense. As we move forward, our focus remains on successfully integrating the two organizations, realizing the strategic benefits of the combination and continuing to serve our customers and communities."

Third Quarter Performance Highlights

  • Net interest income increased by $10.8 million, or 89.2%, to $22.8 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, from $12.1 million for the quarter ended June 30, 2026. Net interest income increased by $11.6 million, or 102.3%, from $11.3 million for the comparable quarter in 2025.
  • Annualized net interest margin was 3.68% for the current quarter, compared to 3.22% in the prior quarter and 3.07% for the comparable quarter in 2025.
  • A provision for credit losses of $6.1 million was recorded for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to $823,000 and $269,000 for the quarters ended June 30, 2026 and September 30, 2025, respectively.
  • Noninterest income increased $3.0 million to $4.6 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $1.6 million for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, and increased $3.3 million from $1.3 million for the comparable quarter in 2025.
  • Noninterest expense increased $9.8 million to $20.0 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, which included $3.0 million in nonrecurring merger-related expenses, compared to $10.2 million for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, and increased $11.9 million from $8.1 million for the comparable quarter in 2025.

Income Statement Summary

Net Interest Income. Net interest income before the provision for credit losses increased $11.6 million to $22.8 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $11.3 million in the third quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily attributable to the merger with Farmers Bancorp, which significantly expanded the Company's interest-earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities. The acquisition also impacted net interest income through the accretion and amortization of fair value adjustments recorded in connection with the transaction.

Annualized net interest margin was 3.68% for the third quarter of 2026, compared to 3.07% for the third quarter of 2025. The increase primarily reflected higher yields and average balances of interest-earning assets resulting from the loan portfolio acquired in the merger, as well as lower average funding costs and a higher volume of noninterest-bearing demand deposits.

Interest Income. Interest income increased $16.7 million to $38.6 million during the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to $21.8 million during the quarter ended September 30, 2025. The increase was primarily due to a $1.02 billion increase in the average balance of interest-earning assets, mainly as a result of the merger with Farmers Bancorp. The average yield on interest-earning assets was 6.20%, compared to 5.93% in the third quarter of 2025.

Interest income on loans and leases increased $14.6 million to $34.3 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to $19.7 million in the third quarter of 2025. This increase was primarily due to an $831.9 million increase in the average balance of loans and leases, mainly reflecting loans acquired in the merger with Farmers Bancorp. The average yield earned on loans and leases was 6.79% as compared to 6.63% in the same quarter a year ago.

Interest income on investment securities, excluding FHLB stock, increased $1.3 million to $2.9 million during the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to the quarter ended September 30, 2025, due to a $110.5 million increase in the average balance of securities and a 66 basis point increase in the average yield to 3.25%. The increases were primarily due to securities acquired in the acquisition and the subsequent repositioning of the securities portfolio. Dividends on FHLB stock increased $203,000 to $517,000 during the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to the quarter ended September 30, 2025, primarily due to a $7.1 million increase in the average balance of FHLB stock held.

Interest income on cash and cash equivalents increased $623,000 to $826,000 during the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to the quarter ended September 30, 2025. The increase from the third quarter of 2025 was primarily due to increased cash balances maintained following the merger with Farmers Bancorp.

Interest Expense. Interest expense increased $5.2 million to $15.7 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to the quarter ended September 30, 2025. The increase was due to a $728.8 million increase in the average balance of interest-bearing liabilities, primarily as a result of the merger with Farmers Bancorp, partially offset by a decrease in the average rate paid. The average rate paid on interest-bearing liabilities during the third quarter of 2026 was 3.17%, compared to 3.35% in the third quarter of 2025.

Interest expense on deposits increased $4.9 million to $12.7 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to the third quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily due to a $710.5 million increase in the average balance of interest-bearing deposits as a result of the merger with Farmers Bancorp, partially offset by a decrease in the average rate paid. The average rate paid on interest-bearing deposits was 2.98% and 3.14% for the quarters ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively.  Within interest-bearing deposits, the average rate paid on interest-bearing checking accounts increased to 2.19% for the third quarter of 2026 compared to 1.17% for the third quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily attributable to public fund accounts acquired in the merger with Farmers Bancorp, which pay higher rates to municipal depositors.

Interest expense on borrowings increased $266,000 to $3.0 million for the third quarter of 2026 compared to the third quarter of 2025. The average balance of borrowings totaled $284.1 million during the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to $265.8 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2025. The increase in the average balance was primarily due to subordinated debt assumed in the merger with Farmers Bancorp. The average rate paid on borrowings was 4.26% for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to 4.16% for the third quarter of 2025.

Provision for Credit Losses. A provision for credit losses of $6.1 million was recorded in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $269,000 in the third quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily due to the need to replenish the allowance following a $4.5 million partial charge-off recorded upon the transfer of a commercial real estate property to other real estate owned and an $803,000 charge-off on a commercial and industrial loan, as well as an increase in non-performing loans during the quarter. The related commercial real estate loan was placed on nonaccrual status in the second quarter of 2026, and the Company took possession of the property late in the third quarter. Net charge-offs for the third quarter of 2026 were $6.1 million, compared to $317,000 in the third quarter of 2025. No provision for credit losses was recorded at acquisition on loans acquired in the merger, as the initial allowance on those loans was established through the gross-up approach described under "Allowance for Credit Losses."

Noninterest Income. Total noninterest income increased $3.3 million to $4.6 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to the quarter ended September 30, 2025. The increase included a $1.6 million preliminary bargain purchase gain in connection with the merger with Farmers Bancorp. Excluding this gain, noninterest income increased $1.6 million, primarily reflecting the larger customer base following the merger, including increases of $415,000 in service charges on deposit accounts and $1.1 million in other income primarily related to wealth management income.

Noninterest Expense. Total noninterest expense increased $11.9 million to $20.0 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the third quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily attributable to the merger with Farmers Bancorp, which significantly expanded the Company's operating infrastructure and employee base. The quarter also included $3.0 million in nonrecurring merger-related expenses, consisting primarily of software and core conversion expenses. In addition, noninterest expense was impacted by $1.8 million in amortization expense related to the core deposit intangible recognized in connection with the merger.

Income Tax Expense. Income tax expense decreased $1.1 million during the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the quarter ended September 30, 2025. The Company recognized an income tax benefit of $482,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to income tax expense of $645,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The $1.1 million decrease was primarily attributable to lower pre-tax income and favorable tax effects from a preliminary bargain purchase gain, higher tax credits and increased tax-exempt interest income, partially offset by nondeductible transaction costs.

Balance Sheet Summary

General. Total assets increased $1.07 billion to $2.60 billion at September 30, 2026, as compared to $1.53 billion at December 31, 2025, primarily due to $1.2 billion in assets acquired from the merger with Farmers Bancorp.

Investment Securities. Investment securities increased $75.1 million to $329.8 million at September 30, 2026, compared to $254.7 million at December 31, 2025. The increase was primarily due to $205.0 million in available for sale securities acquired from the merger with Farmers Bancorp. Offsetting this increase were sales of $91.9 million of securities acquired. The proceeds from sales were used to pay off FHLB advances assumed in the merger.

Loans and Leases. Loans and leases increased $827.2 million to $2.00 billion at September 30, 2026, compared to $1.18 billion at December 31, 2025. The increase was primarily attributable to $803.6 million in loans acquired from the merger with Farmers Bancorp, with the remaining $23.6 million reflecting organic loan growth.

Non-performing loans and leases, consisting of nonaccrual loans and leases and accruing loans and leases 90 days or more past due, totaled $32.2 million, or 1.59% of total loans and leases, at September 30, 2026, compared to $17.4 million, or 1.46%, at December 31, 2025. Nonaccrual loans and leases increased $17.4 million to $30.6 million at September 30, 2026, from $13.2 million at December 31, 2025. The increase in non-performing loans and leases was primarily due to $4.8 million of loans and leases that were non-performing when acquired in the merger with Farmers Bancorp, $1.1 million of acquired loans and leases that became non-performing after the acquisition, and $8.9 million of legacy loans and leases that became non-performing during the period, primarily consisting of commercial and industrial loans associated with one customer relationship. 

Allowance for Credit Losses. The allowance for credit losses on loans and leases increased $8.9 million to $25.4 million, or 1.25% of total loans and leases, at September 30, 2026, from $16.5 million, or 1.38% of total loans and leases, at December 31, 2025. The increase was primarily due to the initial allowance for credit losses of $8.3 million established on loans acquired in the merger with Farmers Bancorp, including $699,000 on purchased credit-deteriorated loans and $7.6 million on purchased seasoned loans, and a provision for credit losses of $7.6 million, partially offset by net charge-offs of $7.0 million during the nine months ended September 30, 2026. The Company early adopted ASU 2025-08, Financial Instruments - Credit Losses  (Topic 326): Purchased Loans, and applied the gross-up approach to the purchased seasoned loans. Under this approach, the initial allowance on those loans was recorded as an adjustment to their amortized cost basis at acquisition, rather than through provision expense. As a result, no day-one provision for credit losses was recognized on loans acquired in the merger. The allowance for credit losses provided coverage of 78.9% of non-performing loans and leases at September 30, 2026, compared to 94.6% at December 31, 2025. The decrease in the allowance as a percentage of total loans and leases primarily reflects lower expected credit loss rates on the acquired loan portfolio relative to the legacy portfolio. The decrease in the allowance as a percentage of non-performing loans and leases primarily reflects the $14.8 million increase in non-performing loans and leases, a significant portion of which are collateral-dependent loans requiring limited specific reserves based on the estimated fair value of the underlying collateral. Net charge-offs for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 were $7.0 million, or an annualized 0.64% of average loans and leases, compared to $1.3 million for the comparable period of 2025.

Management regularly evaluates credit exposure across its loan portfolio and within its geographic markets. As of September 30, 2026, the Company's credit risk assessment incorporated ongoing economic conditions, including inflationary pressures, capital market volatility, and geopolitical risks. Management continues to conduct portfolio stress testing and monitor credit metrics and believes the allowance for credit losses is appropriate based on the current composition of the loan and lease portfolio and the level of individually evaluated reserves.

Other Assets. Other assets increased $66.6 million to $97.6 million at September 30, 2026, compared to $31.0 million at December 31, 2025. The increase was primarily attributable to the merger with Farmers Bancorp, including the recognition of a core deposit intangible asset of $22.9 million, a $20 million increase in the cash surrender value of bank-owned life insurance, a $4.8 million increase in accrued interest receivable and a $1.4 million increase in mortgage servicing rights. At September 30, 2026, the carrying value of the core deposit intangible was $21.2 million.

Included in other assets, other real estate owned totaled $2.7 million at September 30, 2026, compared to $56,000 at December 31, 2025.  The increase was primarily due to the transfer of two commercial real estate properties to other real estate owned during the third quarter of 2026: a former behavioral health hospital campus located in Dayton, Ohio, with a carrying value of $2.2 million, and a restaurant property located in Richmond, Indiana, with a carrying value of $450,000. Both properties were recorded at fair value less estimated costs to sell at the time of transfer.  The Company is actively marketing both properties for sale.

Deposits. Total deposits increased $970.5 million to $2.09 billion at September 30, 2026, compared to $1.11 billion at December 31, 2025. The increase in deposits from December 31, 2025 was primarily due to $935.8 million in deposits acquired from the merger with Farmers Bancorp. Brokered time deposits totaled $268.1 million, or 12.9% of total deposits, at September 30, 2026, compared to $235.9 million, or 21.2% of total deposits at December 31, 2025. Noninterest-bearing demand deposits totaled $351.4 million at September 30, 2026 compared to $100.1 million at December 31, 2025, and were 16.9% and 9.0% of total deposits at September 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025, respectively.

Borrowings. Total borrowings increased $11.6 million to $263.6 million at September 30, 2026, compared to $252.0 million at December 31, 2025. The increase was primarily due to the $14.5 million in subordinated debt assumed in the merger with Farmers Bancorp, partially offset by the repayment of other FHLB advances. The Company also assumed approximately $95 million in FHLB advances in the merger, all of which were repaid during the quarter with proceeds from the sale of available for sale securities acquired in the merger.

Stockholders' Equity. Stockholders' equity totaled $228.9 million at September 30, 2026, an increase of $83.1 million from December 31, 2025. The increase in stockholders' equity was primarily attributable to the issuance of 6,254,286 shares of common stock due to the merger with Farmers Bancorp, resulting in an increase to equity of $99.3 million, and net income of $6.8 million. Offsetting these increases were an increase to other comprehensive loss of $18.5 million, reflecting an increase in net unrealized losses on available-for-sale securities, net of tax, due to higher market interest rates during the period, and $5.3 million in dividends paid to Company stockholders.

data.title: University Bancorp Closes on the Acquisition of 20% of UIF Corporation for Cash & Stock Worth About $15.2 Million
data.description:
ANN ARBOR, MI / ACCESS Newswire / October 30, 2026 / University Bancorp, Inc. (OTCQB:UNIB) or ("UNIB") announced that it closed today on the previously announced transaction to acquire 20% of UIF Corporation. UIF is a key subsidiary of University Bank, previously 80% owned, and now 100% owned by University Bank. The final terms at the closing of the transaction were different than the terms originally negotiated, which originally involved an all-stock stock swap.

In the transaction, UNIB issued 482,054 newly issued shares of UNIB common stock and in addition, paid $3,911,147.50 cash, to acquire the 20% of UIF that it did not already own. At September 30, 2026, UIF had shareholders' equity of $76,050,646. Minority Interest of $15,210,129 as of September 30, 2026 was acquired in the transaction. The acquisition therefore increases the shareholders' equity of UNIB by $11,298,981.70 as of September 30, 2026, had it closed then. The Tier 1 Capital of University Bank increases as a result of the acquisition by about $4 million going forward due to the elimination of the minority interest in UIF.

Shareholders and investors are encouraged to refer to the financial information including the investor presentations, audited financial statements, strategic plan and prior press releases, available on our investor relations web page at: http://www.university-bank.com/bancorp/.

A detailed income statement, balance sheet and other financial information for UNIB and University Bank as of September 30, 2026, is available here: https://www.university-bank.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/3Q2026-UNIB-Detailed-Financial-Information.pdf.
